To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TIMP3 expression in hepatocytes is sufficient to protect against diet-dependent fatty liver disease and tumorigenisis.

hepatocyte specific TIMP-3 overexpression prevents diet-dependent liver disease and hepatocyte-specific loss of ADAM17 improves liver steatosis and prevents liver cancer in diet-dependent mouse models of non-alcoholic fatty liver.
TIMP3 over-expression in hepatocytes prevents diet-induced fatty liver and hepatocellular tumorigenesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of TIMP3 in the development of fatty liver and liver cancer and the mechanisms involved.
the identification of novel molecular targets to treat NAFLD and liver cancer, and the role of ADAM17 in this context.
a better understanding of the role of TIMP3 in liver disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TIMP3 is a key regulator in liver metabolism and tumorigenisis.
the overexpression of TIMP3 in liver cells prevents the progression of NAFL to NASH, and the development of hepatocellular carcinoma, at least in mice.
TIMP3 over-expression is able to improve liver steatosis in mice fed with HFD and to reduce the development of hepatocellular carcinoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hepatocyte-specific TIMPC3 overexpression prevents diet-dependent fatty liver disease and liver cancer, at least in parts, by inhibiting ADAM17.

the hepatocyte specific expression of TIMP3 prevents the progression of diet induced fatty liver disease and hepatic tumorigenicity, at least in a part through the regulation of the activity of ADAM17.
TIMP3 expression is a protective mechanism against NAFLD and liver cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TIMP3 over-expression can prevent the progression of NAFL to NAFLD, at least in mice.
TIMP3 is a potential target to treat NAFLD and HCC.
the inhibition of ADAM17 in liver may represent an effective strategy in the prevention and treatment of NAFLD and hepatocellular cancer.
